property_summary: After any call to Put, Acc[msg.sender].balance must always increase by at least msg.value; the bug removes the balance update, so balance stays unchanged and this rule fails.
After a call to Put with any parameters, Acc[caller].balance must be at least msg.value; the bug removes the balance increment, so it breaks this lower bound for any non-zero msg.value.
After a call to Put, Acc[caller].balance equals the previous balance plus msg.value; the bug omits the addition so balance stays unchanged when msg.value > 0.

After any call to Put with non-zero msg.value, the caller's Acc balance must eventually increase relative to its value before the call; the mutant omits the balance update so the balance never increases regardless of msg.value.

After any sequence culminating in Put, the sum over all Acc[addr].balance must equal or exceed the net msg.value sent into the contract's fallback/Put minus successful Collect withdrawals; the mutant never increments balance, so the invariant fails when msg.value > 0.

After the first call to Put succeeds and completes, a second call to Put (or any nonReentrant_ function) from the same account should always succeed in the correct contract but always fail in the buggy contract because the lock is not released.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the balance of an account in the reference contract equals the sum of all values sent to Put by that account, but the buggy contract prevents this invariant from holding because it allows at most one successful Put per account.
After exactly one successful Put from a caller, a second call to Put from the same caller will succeed in the reference and fail in the buggy contract because the reentrancy lock is never released.

After any sequence of calls to Put from any callers, the Acc[caller].balance of each caller in the reference contract equals the total ether sent by that caller, while in the buggy contract this invariant can be broken because the permanent lock prevents some calls from succeeding and recording their value.
After any successful Put call, the reentrancy lock must be released so that exactly the same caller can immediately initiate a second Put call without reverting due to the lock being held.

After a successful Collect, the contract's balance is always at least as high as the sender's recorded balance in the reference, but the buggy version can violate this invariant when funds are collected before the unlock time.
In the reference contract, a successful Collect must only occur when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime; the buggy version allows Collect to succeed before the unlockTime, violating this invariant.
